body:
I'm testing it out on my demo project which has the advantage of an option to set different output devices in the drop-down box: https://github.com/goatchurchprime/godot-demo-projects/tree/gtch/mic_input/audio/mic_input

I can confirm it is robust in all cases I have tried and restarts without a hiccup. 

The original code says it emits the error `pa_context_get_server_info error: Bad state` every 1000ms from inside the if-statement `if (ad->output_device_name == "Default")` so I don't understand why it is firing when I select an output device that is not `Default`.  https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blame/master/drivers/pulseaudio/audio_driver_pulseaudio.cpp#L509

Aside from that, this essential auto-hot-reconnection feature does throw shade onto my objection to the feature of being able to change the active device while the audio system is running.  My objection was two-fold:
  1. It's not a good idea to have potentially stalling operations inside the real-time audio thread.
  2. There is no good place to report and handle the case of a connection error.

Currently when there is a connection error after changing the output device, the system makes a second attempt to connect to the `Default` output device (whether you want to or not), before entirely closing down the audio system, which is potentially very unhelpful.

There is no feature for turning on or off the Output audio system from GDScript, however there now is for the Input audio system with [Error AudioServer::set_input_device_active(bool p_is_active)](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/servers/audio/audio_server.cpp#L1864) where it is possible to report common connections problems, such as failing to set `audio/driver/enable_input` to true.

I now see that my design isn't helpful in the case of the microphone disconnecting.  If I had my way I would create an input connection error signal callback so we could throw it back to the game designer who could decide what they want to do with the information (eg throw up an in-game warning message that the microphone is disconnected).

As it happens, this PR introduces a second place where `init_input_device()` gets called in the thread with (as it says in the comments) no good way to handle the failure case.

Could we merge the two cases by, say, setting `ad->output_device_name = "Broken"` and then let the `if (ad->output_device_name != ad->new_output_device)` pick up this case and restart in that loop?

(I assume in your last paragraph, `s/output_device/input_device/g`)

I read the code, and I thought this was going to work, but when I tried it, it didn't.  That code only gets reached if pa_stream_get_state(ad->pa_rec_str) == PA_STREAM_READY, but that's not true after a disconnect.

More broadly, I'm in favor of dealing with microphone disconnection better, but (a) my games don't use a microphone so it hasn't come up for me and (b) it could be handled in a separate PR without blocking this improvement.

I did, while testing, notice a couple more bugs, so I'm about to push two more fixes to this branch.  One fixes an assertion failure in pulseaudio which causes Godot to exit; I'm pretty sure I got it but it's a little tricky to trigger. In theory, that could be a separate PR, and if folks prefer that, I can do that -- but it's also only three lines.
I don't mean to pester, but I would love to get some review on this. Is there something I can do to help the process along?

Pestering is the only way to get stuff to happen sometimes.   I'll have a look now.  
You could also come to the AudioGroup meeting (see rocket chat channel) in 2.5 hours if you can make it.

My brief proposal would be as follows:

Whereas `Main::setup()` calls [audio_server->init()](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d569fcf207aea355ea9d0822255ad490945f5572/main/main.cpp#L3590) followed by [audio_server->load_default_bus_layout()](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d569fcf207aea355ea9d0822255ad490945f5572/main/main.cpp#L3877),
and `Main::cleanup()` calls [audio_server->finish()](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d569fcf207aea355ea9d0822255ad490945f5572/main/main.cpp#L5322), 

(1) We would make a new function called: `AudioServer.restart()` which would store the current bus layout by calling `AudioServer::generate_bus_layout()`, then call `audio_server->finish()` followed by `audio_server->init()` and `AudioServer::set_bus_layout()`.

(2) The state of the AudioServer would either be working, or broken (with a reported error state).

(3) All Audio Driver restart code would be deleted from the audio thread.

(4) Every possible change to the audio system configuration would be possible at runtime, and you wouldn't even need to restart the engine when connecting a surround sound system.

(5) The downside is that all the audio effect instance objects would be invalidated.  (This is another reason to move the AudioEffects from busses to the `AudioStreamPlayer`s.)

Discussed in the audio meeting.
While nobody had significant concerns, and this probably is an improvement over the status quo, we don't have any experts (i'm aware of) that could greenlight this approach.

The two main issues should definitely be addressed (error spam and crash), and we can do this in separate PRs (edit: merged https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/119977 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/119975).

The change I'd personally be willing to greenlight is low-level functions that would allow people to implement this themselves if they wanted (e.g. a function to restart the audio system, and a signal that lets users know when connection failed). 
Ultimately, we'd like for the engine to be robust, but the low-level solution will always be correct no matter in what way the engine handles its own failures since there will always be pro users who might want to implement their own solutions, replacing/amending the engine ones.
